name: pkey_mprotect
synopsis: int pkey_mprotect(void *addr, size_t len, int prot, int pkey);
description: pkey_mprotect changes the protection on specified memory pages and assigns a protection key. It requires the protection key to be allocated via pkey_alloc beforehand. This allows for fine-grained access control using memory protection keys.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory region to protect; must be page-aligned

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the memory region in bytes

parameters.name: prot
parameters.description: Protection flags, such as PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, or PROT_EXEC

parameters.name: pkey
parameters.description: Protection key to assign to the memory; must be allocated with pkey_alloc

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The memory cannot be given the specified access, e.g., due to read-only file mapping
addr is not a valid pointer or not a multiple of the system page size
pkey has not been allocated with pkey_alloc(2)
Both PROT_GROWSUP and PROT_GROWSDOWN were specified in prot
Insufficient kernel memory, invalid addresses in the range, or exceeds mapping limits
